source_text: Sed si hoc fingatur ambiguum, te continuo crassissima dubii nubes involvet. Hac quippe concupiscentia carnis nullum absolute genitalium tenetur indicium. Dicam ergo aures hoc vocabulo variorum sitientes carminum verberari, dicam castigari a sancto Ioanne helluonum palatum, dicam culpari immorientes odoribus nares; totum postremo praeter id quod tu arbitraris; libera est electio, ubi specialis verbi nulla pressura est. Aut ergo nega illa quae diximus concupisci; et inficiare, ut soles, omnium conscientiae; aut si necdum eo usque impudentia incalluit, ut his conetur obniti, assentire damnationem genitalis iucunditatis nec in sermonibus inveniri.
pass_a_gloss: But if this be feigned ambiguous, a very thick cloud of doubt will immediately wrap you. For by this desire of the flesh no indication of the genitals is held absolutely. I will say therefore that by this word ears thirsting for various songs are beaten, I will say that the palate of gluttons is chastised by holy John, I will say that nostrils dying upon odors are blamed; finally everything except that which you think; the choice is free, where there is no pressure of a special word. Either therefore deny that those things which we have said are desired; and disown, as you are accustomed, the conscience of all; or if shamelessness has not yet grown so hard that it tries to resist these, assent that the condemnation of genital delight is not found even in the speeches.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: Even if we pretend that this is uncertain, the thickest cloud of doubt will immediately envelop you. For this phrase, “desire of the flesh,” contains absolutely no indication of the reproductive organs. I can therefore say that this expression strikes at ears thirsting for different songs; I can say that Saint John rebukes the glutton’s palate; I can say that he blames nostrils dying for perfumes. In short, I can say anything except what you suppose. The choice is open when no specific word imposes a restriction. Either deny, then, that people desire the things I have named, and contradict everyone’s awareness, as you usually do; or, if your shamelessness has not yet hardened enough to resist these facts, admit that a condemnation of sexual pleasure is not found even in the words.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
